title: kv-cache-management-investigation-2026-03
content:
Summary:

This doc captures an internal investigation into KV (key-value) cache management behavior across typical inference workloads. We focused on reuse rates, eviction patterns, paging between GPU and host, and memory-bandwidth bottlenecks. Experiments were run on a NVIDIA A100 (40GB) equivalent cluster with our production serving runtime (commit a1b2c3) and representative prompt distributions (chatty short-turn, long-context summarization).

Goals:
- Measure KV reuse rates by workload (turn length, sequence length distribution, batch size).
- Identify eviction behavior and how it correlates with latency anomalies and throughput drops.
- Quantify paging overhead when KV spills to host memory and when GPUDirect/tracking prefetch is used.
- Attribute CPU/GPU memory bandwidth usage during heavy KV activity and identify hotspots.
- Propose mitigations (policy, instrumentation, prefetching, caching heuristics).

Testbed and methodology:
- Runtime: serving-runtime commit a1b2c3; KV cache codepath with LRU eviction and reference counting enabled.
- Models: 7B and 13B transformer models (FP16) with per-layer KV caching enabled.
- Workloads:
  - chat-short: median user turn 32 tokens, history 6 turns (reuse expected).
  - chat-long: median user turn 64 tokens, history 30 turns (high KV size).
  - summarization: single long document 4096 tokens (large KV footprint, limited reuse).
- Configs: batch sizes {1,4,8}, max_seq {512,1024,4096}, kv_cache_capacity tuned by entries and bytes.
- Tools: nvprof/ncu to sample memory bandwidth and kernel times, perf for CPU-side activity, our runtime counters (kv_cache_hits_total, kv_cache_misses_total, kv_evictions_total, kv_prefetch_bytes_total).
- Each run: 1000 requests, warmup 100, collect p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and telemetry.

Key findings:
1) Reuse rates are workload-dependent and highly sensitive to batching.
   - chat-short: reuse_rate ~ 68% at batch=1, increases to ~78% at batch=4 (more requests share prefixes).
   - chat-long: reuse_rate drops to ~34% at batch=1 and ~42% at batch=4. Large history reduces prefix overlap and increases KV size causing more frequent evictions.
   - summarization: reuse_rate <10% because each request has unique long context.

2) Eviction churn correlates with throughput regressions and p99 spikes.
   - High eviction rate (>150 evictions/min) observed for chat-long when kv capacity < 28GB. Evictions cause repeated recomputation of KV for tokens that would otherwise be reused.
   - p99 latency increased by 2.1x when eviction_churn > threshold; root cause is extra attention KV generation kernels plus memory copies for refilling cache.

3) Paging (GPU->host and back) introduces large tail latency and consumes significant PCIe/NVLink bandwidth when the KV set exceeds device memory.
   - When KV spills to host (policy: spill-to-host), we measured average additional latency per request +45ms (batch=4, 13B model) and p99 +120ms.
   - nvprof shows sustained PCIe bandwidth of 12-16 GB/s during heavy spill operations; this competes with other device-host traffic (e.g., embedding upload).

4) Memory bandwidth is a real limiter for KV-heavy workloads on larger models.
   - Kernel timelines show KV read/write linear with KV size; memory-bound kernels (KV scatter/gather, KV read) dominate wall time when sequence lengths > 1024.
   - A100 sustained device memory bandwidth measurements during worst-case runs reached ~320 GB/s of DRAM traffic (close to hardware capability for hot kernels).

Measurements (representative numbers):
- chat-short, 7B, batch=4: reuse_rate 78%, kv_evictions_total 12/min, throughput 230 reqs/s, p99 28ms.
- chat-long, 13B, batch=4: reuse_rate 42%, kv_evictions_total 176/min, throughput 60 reqs/s, p99 210ms (vs baseline 98ms when kv capacity doubled).
- summarization, 13B, batch=1, seq=4096: reuse_rate 6%, kv_evictions_total 420/min, sustained PCIe 14 GB/s, p99 420ms.

Analysis and hypotheses:
- Eviction policy (pure LRU) is suboptimal for workloads with bursty long histories: older but hot prefixes get evicted when cache capacity is accounted in raw bytes. We suspect an LFU+aging policy would retain frequently used KV entries across conversations.
- Current entry sizing is coarse (per-token fixed bytes), causing over-allocation when quantization differences or layer-specific sparsity could reduce footprint. Dynamic per-entry sizing could improve density.
- Paging overhead is exacerbated by synchronous fetch semantics. When a request triggers a miss, we synchronously pull back the KV from host and stall the request; this blocks the GPU and increases tail. Asynchronous prefetch + reservation (pin a small working set) could hide PCIe latency.
- Memory bandwidth saturation from large KV reads benefits from packing contiguous reads and reducing scatter/gather kernel overhead. Kernel fusion / vectorized reads may reduce DRAM traffic.

Proposed mitigations (short-term):
- Increase default KV capacity headroom for chat-long workloads (config knob per deployment tier). Test results show doubling KV capacity reduces evictions and p99 by ~2x for chat-long.
- Implement LFU-with-aging prototype (prefer entries with frequent hits, but decay counts over time). Add an 'importance' score = hits * recency_factor to reduce eviction of frequently used conversation prefixes.
- Add asynchronous host-prefetch path: on eviction/miss, schedule a background prefetch and mark request as "degraded" and route to an alternative (e.g., smaller model) if prefetch latency > threshold.
- Enable per-layer compressed KV representation (4-bit/8-bit pack) for layers that tolerate quantization; reduces device memory pressure.

Instrumentation and telemetry to add (actionable metrics):
- kv_cache_hit_ratio by model_id and route (labels): p50/p95 per-minute.
- kv_eviction_churn (evictions/min) and evicted_entry_age distribution.
- kv_paging_bytes_in/out and kv_paging_latency histogram.
- kv_prefetch_success_rate and prefetch_latency histogram.
- per-kernel memory bandwidth sampling exported to traces for correlation with p99 spikes.

Operational notes and quick wins:
- For Dedicated customers experiencing p99 spikes: recommend increasing reserved KV capacity or enabling compressed-KV flag. These are low-risk config changes.
- Add an alert: kv_eviction_churn > 100/min AND p99_latency_model > baseline*1.5 triggers an ops investigation.

Open questions and next experiments:
- How does LFU-with-aging compare to LRU under steady-state multi-tenant workloads? Need a 24h stress run with mixed tenants and hitting patterns.
- What's the max achievable reduction by per-layer compression without quality regressions? Run automatic evals against representative prompts and track generation quality metrics.
- Can we implement an intra-GPU prefetch ring-buffer that keeps the last N KV entries in a contiguous GPU buffer to reduce scatter/gather overhead? Prototype on a single node and re-measure memory bandwidth.

Next steps (owners and timeline):
- Prototype LFU-with-aging and run 48h mixed-tenant stress test (Owner: Samir, ETA: 3w).
- Implement asynchronous prefetch demo and measure p99 impact on chat-long traffic (Owner: Lena, ETA: 2w).
- Add telemetry counters to runtime and instrument dashboards (Owner: Ravi, ETA: 1w).

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Check INF-4823 for prior discussion about compressed KV and link to PR #78 for kernel fusion experiments.
- Share these findings in serving-runtime weekly sync and propose prioritization for the prefetch work.

End of notes.
